**Alison Espach** (born September 26, 1984) is an American novelist. Espach is the author of three novels— _The Adults_ (2011), _Notes on Your Sudden Disappearance_ (2022), and _[The Wedding People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wedding_People "The Wedding People")_ (2024). She is a professor of English at [Providence College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College") in Rhode Island.
## Biography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]
Espach was born in [Trumbull, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trumbull,_Connecticut "Trumbull, Connecticut"), on September 26, 1984.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-Patch_2011-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-2) She is a 2007 graduate of [Providence College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College") in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where English professor [Peter Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Johnson_\(poet\) "Peter Johnson \(poet\)") was a mentor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-PC_News_2016-3)
After graduation, she pursued a [Master of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts") at [Washington University in St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_University_in_St._Louis "Washington University in St. Louis"), Missouri, during which she wrote a thesis that would become her first novel, _The Adults_ (2011). She moved to New York to teach writing after completing the program.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-Patch_2011-1) In 2013, she joined the faculty of Providence College.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-PC_News_2016-3) She is a professor of English.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-4)
## Novels
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Novels")]
###  _The Adults_ (2011)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Adults \(2011\)")]
_The Adults_ is a novel centered on a teenage girl growing up in a small, wealthy town in Connecticut.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-NYT_Maslin_2011-5) It was published by [Charles Scribner's Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Scribner's_Sons "Charles Scribner's Sons") in early 2011.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-6)
In the _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times")_ , literary critic [Janet Maslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Maslin "Janet Maslin")'s review characterized the work as a "[coming of age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_of_age_story "Coming of age story") with a quick wit and a sharp eye".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-NYT_Maslin_2011-5) _[Kirkus Reviews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkus_Reviews "Kirkus Reviews")_ found the work to be "an enviable first effort."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-7) [Dreamscape Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamscape_Media "Dreamscape Media") produced an audiobook, which was read by Tavia Gilbert; her narration was received positively by _[AudioFile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AudioFile_\(magazine\) "AudioFile \(magazine\)")_ magazine, with its reviewer writing that "Subtle shifts of tone are all Gilbert needs to give Emily a convincing voice".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-8)
Film producers [Jamie Patricof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Patricof "Jamie Patricof") and [Lynette Howell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynette_Howell "Lynette Howell"), of Electric City Entertainment, [optioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optioned "Optioned") the rights to the novel in 2012.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-9)
###  _Notes on Your Sudden Disappearance_ (2022)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Notes on Your Sudden Disappearance \(2022\)")]
Espach's second novel depicts a family following the death of its eldest child. _[Kirkus Reviews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkus_Reviews "Kirkus Reviews")_ described it as a "tragicomic bildungsroman in the shadow of loss".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-10)
[Henry Holt and Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Holt_and_Company "Henry Holt and Company")'s hardcover design features a 2016 painting, "The Swimming Pool", by T. S. Harris from the stock photo website [Bridgeman Images](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeman_Images "Bridgeman Images"), while the paperback features a commercial stock photo of flowers behind the typography.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-11) [Macmillan Audio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macmillan_Audio "Macmillan Audio") released an audiobook adaptation narrated by Jesse Vilinsky.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-12)
###  _The Wedding People_ (2024)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: The Wedding People \(2024\)")]
Main article: [The Wedding People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wedding_People "The Wedding People")
In Espach's third novel, _[The Wedding People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wedding_People "The Wedding People")_ , Phoebe Stone travels to a hotel in [Newport, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport,_Rhode_Island "Newport, Rhode Island") to enjoy one last night of self-indulgence before killing herself by drug overdose. Her planned suicide is averted when she befriends the bride of a wedding being held at the hotel. _The Wedding People_ appeared on the [_New York Times_ Best Seller list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list") and won the fiction category in the 2024 [Goodreads Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodreads_Choice_Awards "Goodreads Choice Awards").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-Boston_Globe_12-2024-13) It was shortlisted for the 'Published Novels' section of the 2025 [Comedy Women in Print Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Women_in_Print_Prize "Comedy Women in Print Prize").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-14) It is a finalist for the 2025 [Thurber Prize for American Humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thurber_Prize_for_American_Humor "Thurber Prize for American Humor").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-15)
Prior to its publication, in early 2024, [TriStar Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TriStar_Pictures "TriStar Pictures") was reported to have acquired rights to a film adaption of the novel, naming [Will Speck and Josh Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Speck_and_Josh_Gordon "Will Speck and Josh Gordon") as directors and [Nicole Holofcener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Holofcener "Nicole Holofcener") as writer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-16) _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ columnist [John Warner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Warner_\(writer\) "John Warner \(writer\)") found _The Wedding People_ to be a "highly recommended, deeply satisfying read."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-17) A _[Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Post "Washington Post")_ review of the audiobook adaption, narrated by Helen Laser, highlighted Laser's versatility in voicing the various characters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-18)
